task.statement: The roman package exposes is_roman_numeral (already implemented) and a stub to_roman(n). Implement to_roman(n) so that it converts an integer n in the range 1..3999 inclusive to its standard Roman numeral string using subtractive notation (4='IV', 9='IX', 40='XL', 90='XC', 400='CD', 900='CM'). Return a str. Raise ValueError when n is an int outside 1..3999. Raise TypeError when n is not an int (for example '5', 5.0, None, [1]); numeric strings and integral floats are not coerced. Type discipline is by value: an instance of an int subclass (for example an IntEnum member or `class PlainInt(int)`) is accepted and converted exactly like the int with the same value, including the range check. Int subclasses that override arithmetic or comparison operators are out of scope: their behaviour is unspecified and tests must not depend on it. bool is a subclass of int; rejecting True and False with TypeError is permitted but not required, and tests must not depend on either choice. Do not change is_roman_numeral or the tests.
